Bundled FFmpeg runtime: n6.1.4
Source commit: 34277e12e80031c7f89494ba543684bc1dd0be8f
Source: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg
The matching unmodified source snapshot is ffmpeg-n6.1.4-source.tar.xz.

Configure arguments:
--enable-shared --disable-static --disable-programs --disable-doc --disable-debug
--disable-everything --enable-avcodec --enable-avutil --enable-swscale
--enable-decoder=h264,hevc,av1 --enable-parser=h264,hevc,av1
--enable-hwaccel=h264_vaapi,hevc_vaapi,av1_vaapi --enable-vaapi --enable-vulkan
--enable-libdrm --disable-x86asm --disable-xlib

Since 1.0.0-rc4 the AV1 decoder, parser and VA-API hardware acceleration are enabled
for the optional AV1 stream. FFmpeg's native AV1 decoder decodes only through hardware
acceleration (no software AV1 decoder is included), so AV1 needs a GPU with hardware
AV1 decode; H.264 and HEVC are unchanged. --disable-xlib keeps the
libraries independent of X11 (VA-API uses DRM render nodes), as the earlier builds were.

The environment build also specified a prefix plus include/library search paths
for user-extracted Ubuntu development packages. No source changes were made.
The packaged libraries have RUNPATH $ORIGIN, set with patchelf, to load their
matching adjacent libavutil. See scripts/Build-FFmpeg-Linux.sh for the rebuild.
No GPL components were enabled; the configure result is LGPL 2.1 or later.
These are shared libraries and can be replaced with compatible rebuilt versions.
